name: Autumn Harvest
summary: Squash, apples, mushrooms, lentils, kale and beets, cooked the way autumn calls for: roast squash with lentils, apple-mustard chicken, a creamy mushroom and barley soup and baked apples with oats. Three dishes cook once and make the next day's lunch.
howItWorks:
**Cook once, eat twice.** Monday's squash and lentils, Wednesday's apple-mustard chicken and Thursday's mushroom soup each make two portions, so Tuesday, Thursday and Friday lunches are done. Cool the second portion within 1 hour, keep it up to 3 days and reheat it once to 74 °C, adding yogurt, nuts and seeds cold. Wash all produce before cutting, oranges and lemons too.

**Fish and protein.** Salmon on Tuesday and trout on Saturday are cooked fresh. Canned salmon, with its soft bones, goes into Monday's and Wednesday's salads for **omega-3, calcium and vitamin D**. Chicken, beef, eggs (two breakfasts, three lunches), lentils, chickpeas, white beans, Greek yogurt and milk carry the protein at every other meal.

**Autumn, whole-food carbs.** Squash, apples, mushrooms, beets and kale turn up all week, with oats, barley, buckwheat, potatoes and sweet potatoes as the starch. There is no bread, rice or pasta. A cranberry-orange yogurt bowl and baked apples keep breakfasts sweet.

**Light.** It drops the second snack each day. At 1,400 it roughly halves the fresh salmon, trout and chicken, so they are **modest pieces beside a full plate of vegetables**, and trims the grains, potatoes, beans, lentils, nuts and oil, and a little of the canned salmon and beef. The eggs, sweet potatoes, vegetables and fruit stay as written at 1,400.

**Big.** It adds a third snack a day and grows the grains, potatoes, sweet potatoes, meat, fish, beans, yogurt and milk, with a third egg in some egg dishes. Vegetables and fruit stay as written.

recipes.name: Gingerbread pear overnight oats with walnuts
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by gingerbread and Bircher muesli, with grated pear in place of the usual apple
recipes.about: Rolled oats soaked overnight with grated pear, ginger, cinnamon and a little nutmeg, so it tastes like gingerbread without the sugar. The oats bring **slow fibre**, the milk adds protein and calcium, and the walnuts and pumpkin seeds give it a crunch.
steps: Stir the oats, milk, ginger, cinnamon and nutmeg together in a jar or container with a lid.
Wash the pear, grate it on the coarse side of a grater and fold it in. Cover and chill overnight, or at least 6 hours.
In the morning, stir well. Eat it cold, or warm it in the microwave until just steaming. Loosen with a splash of milk if it has thickened.
Top with the walnuts and pumpkin seeds just before eating so they stay crunchy.
recipes.tip: Soaked oats keep up to 3 days covered in the fridge, never on the counter. Mix a jar the night before and eat it the next morning, or mix two jars at once and eat the second within 3 days.

recipes.name: Warm cranberry-orange compote yogurt bowl with oat crunch
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by the cranberry sauce on a harvest table, made lighter and served over yogurt
recipes.about: Tart cranberries simmered with chopped orange, a little honey and cinnamon until they burst, spooned over cool Greek yogurt with toasted oats, walnuts and pumpkin seeds. Cranberries and orange bring **vitamin C**, and the yogurt carries the protein.

ingredients.note: peeled and chopped, with any juice

steps: Rinse fresh cranberries, and wash, peel and chop the orange. Put the cranberries, chopped orange with its juice, honey and cinnamon in a small pot over medium heat. Simmer 6 to 7 minutes, stirring now and then, until the berries burst and the juice turns syrupy. Let it cool a few minutes.
While it simmers, toast the oats in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3 minutes until golden and nutty. Add the chopped walnuts and pumpkin seeds for the last minute.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, pour the warm compote over and scatter the oat crunch on top.
recipes.tip: Make a double batch of compote and use the second half within 3 days, covered in the fridge. Frozen cranberries need no thawing.

recipes.name: Beet and potato breakfast hash with firm eggs
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by New England red flannel hash, without the corned beef
recipes.about: Crisp-edged potato and ruby beet with soft onion and two eggs cooked until the yolks are firm, finished with parsley and a splash of vinegar. The eggs bring **choline and protein**, and the beets bring folate.
steps: Put the diced potato in a microwave-safe bowl with a splash of water, cover and microwave 4 to 5 minutes, until nearly tender.

Warm the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add the potato and the finely chopped onion and cook 6 minutes, turning now and then, until golden. Add the beets, paprika, a pinch of iodized salt and pepper and cook 3 minutes more.
Make a well in the hash for each egg and crack them in. Cover and cook 6 to 7 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are completely firm. Break the yolks up with a fork if you like.
Finish with the vinegar and the chopped parsley.
recipes.tip: Make it quicker by boiling extra potatoes at dinner the night before. Cool them within 1 hour in a shallow container, refrigerate, use within 3 days and skip the microwave step.

recipes.name: Baked apples stuffed with oats, walnuts and cinnamon
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by the old-fashioned baked apple, with an oat and walnut filling and a spoon of yogurt
recipes.about: A whole apple baked until soft, filled with cinnamon oats, honey and walnuts, with cool Greek yogurt on the side. The oats and apple skin give you **fibre that keeps you full**, and the whole kitchen smells like autumn.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F). Wash the apples, slice a thin lid off the top and scoop out the core with a spoon, keeping the base and sides intact.
Stir the oats, walnuts, honey, cinnamon and a splash of water together into a thick, damp filling. Pack it into the apples and set the lids back on.
Stand the apples in a small baking dish with a splash of water in the bottom. Cover loosely with foil and bake 30 minutes.
Uncover and bake 5 minutes more, until the apples are soft when pierced and the oats are lightly crisp on top.
Serve warm with the cool yogurt.
recipes.tip: The oven does all the work, so put them in and make your coffee. Bake as many apples as you have people.

recipes.name: Beet, apple and white bean salad with canned salmon, a firm egg and walnuts
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Scandinavian beet, apple and fish salads, with white beans to make it a lunch
recipes.about: Sweet beet, crisp apple and creamy white beans over peppery arugula with flaked canned salmon, a firm egg and a sharp mustard-lemon dressing. The salmon brings **omega-3 and calcium from its soft bones**, the egg adds choline, and the beans bring iron, with lemon to help absorb it.

ingredients.note: cooked, vacuum-packed or boiled at home
drained, skin and soft bones left in

steps: Put the egg in a small pot of cold water, bring to a boil and simmer 10 to 11 minutes until the yolk is completely firm. Cool in cold water, then peel.
Whisk the mustard, lemon juice, olive oil, a pinch of iodized salt and pepper with a spoonful of water.
Wash the arugula and apple. Slice the apple thinly and cut the beets into wedges.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 to 3 minutes.
Toss the beans, beets and apple with half the dressing. Pile onto the arugula, flake the salmon over the top, add the quartered egg and the walnuts and spoon over the rest of the dressing.
recipes.tip: Beets stain, so use a board you do not mind. Keep an opened tin covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days. Packing it? Keep the dressing separate and use a cold bag with an ice pack, and eat it the same day.

recipes.name: Roast squash with green lentils, kale and walnuts
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by French-style warm lentil salads, with sage-roasted butternut
recipes.about: Sage-roasted butternut squash on warm lentils with garlicky kale, a mustard and cider vinegar dressing and toasted walnuts and pumpkin seeds. The lentils and squash give you **iron, folate and plenty of fibre**, and the second portion is even better the next day.

ingredients.note: peeled and cut in 2 cm cubes

steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash, peel and cube the squash, then toss it on a tray with half the oil, the sage, a pinch of iodized salt and pepper. Roast about 25 minutes, turning once, until tender and caramelized at the edges.
Meanwhile, rinse the lentils and simmer them with the thyme in plenty of water for 18 to 20 minutes, until tender with a little bite. Drain well.

Slice the onion and soften it in the rest of the oil in a wide skillet for 4 minutes. Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the washed, stemmed and chopped kale with a splash of water. Cook 4 minutes until tender.
Fold the drained lentils into the kale and stir in the mustard and cider vinegar. Taste and add a pinch more iodized salt if it needs it.
Toast the walnuts and pumpkin seeds in a dry pan for 3 minutes. Pile the lentils onto plates and top with the squash and nuts.

This makes two portions. Cool the second portion within 1 hour in a shallow container and refrigerate it for tomorrow's lunch. Reheat the lentils and squash once, until steaming hot, to 74 °C (165 °F), and add the walnuts and seeds cold.
recipes.tip: Keep the second portion up to 3 days in the fridge. Reheat it only once.

recipes.name: Horseradish salmon with roasted Brussels sprouts, carrots and buckwheat
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Scandinavian salmon with horseradish and dill, with autumn vegetables roasted alongside
recipes.about: A salmon fillet roasted beside caramelized Brussels sprouts and carrots, with nutty buckwheat and a sharp horseradish and parsley yogurt sauce. The salmon brings **omega-3, vitamin D and choline**, and the sprouts bring vitamin K and vitamin C.

ingredients.note: washed, peeled and cut in thick batons

steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Toss the Brussels sprouts and carrots on a large tray with most of the oil, a pinch of iodized salt and pepper. Roast 25 minutes, turning once, until browned at the edges and tender.
Meanwhile, rinse the buckwheat and simmer it in about twice its volume of water with a lid on for 12 minutes. Take it off the heat and let it steam 5 minutes.
Stir the yogurt, horseradish, chopped parsley and lemon juice together. Add a spoonful of water if it is too thick.

About 12 minutes before the vegetables are done, pat the salmon dry, rub with the last of the oil, salt and pepper, and set it skin side down on a second small tray. Roast 10 to 12 minutes, until the thickest part reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and flakes easily.
Wash your hands, board and knife with hot soapy water after handling the raw fish.
Fluff the buckwheat with a fork. Serve the salmon on the buckwheat with the vegetables and the sauce.
recipes.tip: Buy the salmon the day you cook it, or thaw frozen fillets in the fridge overnight.

recipes.name: Apple-mustard chicken with red cabbage, white beans and buckwheat
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Polish and German braised cabbage with apple, and Eastern European kasha
recipes.about: Tender chicken thigh pieces simmered with red cabbage, apple, white beans, caraway and mustard, served over nutty buckwheat. The cabbage and apple bring **vitamin C and fibre**, and the chicken and beans bring protein, iron and zinc.
steps: Toss the chicken pieces with the mustard, a pinch of iodized salt and pepper. Rinse the buckwheat, then simmer it in about twice its volume of water with a lid on for 12 minutes. Take it off the heat and let it steam 5 minutes.

Warm half the oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat and brown the chicken for 5 minutes, turning, until golden. It will not be cooked through yet. Move it to a clean plate, and wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken.

In the same skillet, soften the onion in the rest of the oil for 4 minutes. Add the garlic and caraway for 30 seconds. Stir in the washed cabbage, the apple, vinegar and broth, cover and cook 10 minutes until the cabbage is soft.
Return the chicken and any juices to the pan, add the drained beans and simmer uncovered 5 to 6 minutes, until the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) and the sauce has thickened.
Fluff the buckwheat with a fork and stir in the chopped parsley. Serve the chicken and cabbage over it.
This makes two portions. Cool the second portion within 1 hour in a shallow container and refrigerate it for tomorrow's lunch. Reheat it once, until steaming hot, to 74 °C (165 °F).
recipes.tip: Keep the second portion up to 3 days in the fridge and reheat it only once.

recipes.name: Creamy mushroom, barley and white bean soup with spinach
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Polish and Russian mushroom and barley soups, thickened with mashed white beans and a splash of milk instead of cream
recipes.about: Deeply browned mushrooms, chewy barley and white beans, seasoned with thyme and a little caraway. Half the beans are mashed in and a splash of milk makes the broth creamy, then spinach and a squeeze of lemon finish it. The mushrooms bring **B vitamins and copper**, the milk brings calcium, and the beans and barley bring fibre.
steps: Heat a large pot over medium-high heat, add the mushrooms and cook 5 minutes without much stirring, until the water has gone and they are well browned.
Add the oil, chopped onion and carrot and cook 3 minutes. Stir in the garlic, thyme and caraway for 30 seconds.

Add the rinsed barley, a pinch of iodized salt and enough broth and boiling water from the kettle to cover by about 3 cm. Bring back to a boil, then simmer with a lid on 20 minutes, until the barley is tender with a little chew.

Stir in the beans. Mash about half of them against the side of the pot to make the soup creamy. Add the spinach and cook 2 minutes until wilted. Pour in the milk and warm gently for 2 minutes without boiling, then take the pot off the heat and stir in the lemon juice and pepper.
Ladle into bowls, swirl in the yogurt and scatter the chopped walnuts and almonds on top.

This makes two portions. Cool the second portion within 1 hour in a shallow container (barley keeps absorbing broth, so loosen it with water when you reheat). Refrigerate for tomorrow's lunch and reheat gently, without a hard boil, until steaming hot, to 74 °C (165 °F).
recipes.tip: Put the kettle on before you start. The soup keeps up to 3 days in the fridge. Swirl in the yogurt and scatter the nuts on after reheating.

recipes.name: Sage beef strips with sweet potato, kale and white beans
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by a Tuscan-style skillet of beans and greens, with sweet potato and sage for autumn
recipes.about: Quick-seared beef strips in one skillet with crisp-edged sweet potato, wilted kale and creamy white beans, all pulled together with sage and a little mustard. The beef brings **iron and zinc**, and the sweet potato brings vitamin A.

ingredients.note: sliced across the grain in thin strips

steps: Warm half the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the sweet potato with a splash of water, cover and cook 8 minutes until nearly tender, then uncover and cook 6 minutes more, stirring, until browned at the edges. Move it to a plate.

Pat the beef dry and toss with the sage, a pinch of iodized salt and pepper. Add the rest of the oil to the hot skillet and sear the beef in a single layer for 2 to 3 minutes, turning, until browned, with no pink left and at least 71 °C (160 °F) in the thickest strip. Move it to a clean plate, and wash your hands, the board and the knife with hot soapy water after handling the raw beef.

Add the sliced onion to the skillet for 2 minutes, then the garlic for 30 seconds. Add the washed, stemmed and chopped kale, the broth, vinegar and mustard and cook 3 to 4 minutes until the kale is tender.
Stir in the beans, sweet potato and beef and heat through for 2 minutes until steaming. Taste and add a little more vinegar if it needs brightness.
recipes.tip: Put the beef in the freezer for 20 minutes before slicing for thin, even strips. If it was frozen, thaw it in the fridge and use it within 2 days.

recipes.name: Roast squash and chickpea bowl with arugula, firm eggs and tahini-lemon sauce
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Middle Eastern roast pumpkin and chickpea salads with tahini
recipes.about: Cumin and paprika roast butternut and chickpeas on a bed of peppery arugula with firm eggs, a lemony tahini sauce and crunchy walnuts and pumpkin seeds. The chickpeas, eggs and tahini bring **protein, choline, calcium and magnesium** to a bowl that is mostly squash.

ingredients.note: peeled and cut in 2 cm cubes

steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash, peel and cube the squash. Toss it and the drained chickpeas on a tray with the oil, cumin, paprika and a pinch of iodized salt. Roast 25 minutes, turning once, until the squash is tender and the chickpeas are crisp at the edges.
Meanwhile, put the eggs in a small pot of cold water, bring to a boil and simmer 10 to 11 minutes until the yolks are completely firm. Cool in cold water and peel.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, grated garlic and a few spoonfuls of water into a smooth, pourable sauce. Thinly slice the onion, wash the arugula and chop the walnuts and pumpkin seeds.
Pile the arugula into bowls, top with the warm squash and chickpeas, the onion and the halved eggs, then drizzle with the sauce and scatter the walnuts and pumpkin seeds over.
recipes.tip: Roast the chickpeas on the same tray as the squash, then eat the bowl warm or at room temperature. Packing it? Keep the eggs and sauce in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.

recipes.name: Walnut-crusted trout with roasted Brussels sprouts, crisp kale and crushed potatoes
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by nut-crusted fish plates, with a mustard and parsley walnut crust
recipes.about: A rainbow trout fillet under a mustard, parsley and walnut crust, roasted alongside caramelized Brussels sprouts, crisp kale and golden potatoes. The trout brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the walnuts add more omega-3 and a good crunch.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Toss the potatoes on a large tray with half the oil, a pinch of iodized salt and pepper. Roast 8 minutes.
Add the Brussels sprouts and garlic to the tray, toss and roast 17 minutes more, turning once.
Mix the walnuts, chopped parsley and a little oil into a crumbly crust. Pat the trout dry and brush the top with the mustard. Press the crust on firmly and set it on a lined tray.
Wash your hands, board and knife with hot soapy water after handling the raw fish.

Put the trout in the oven for the last 12 minutes, until the thickest part reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and flakes easily. Add the washed, torn kale to the vegetables for the last 6 minutes, until crisp at the edges.
Squeeze the lemon over the trout and vegetables and serve.
recipes.tip: Buy the trout the day you cook it, or thaw frozen fillets in the fridge overnight.

recipes.name: Canned salmon and chickpea salad with apple, red cabbage, spinach and sunflower seeds
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Scandinavian fish and apple salads, with chickpeas for body
recipes.about: Flaked canned salmon and chickpeas with crisp red cabbage, carrot and apple on a big bed of spinach, topped with walnuts and sunflower seeds, in a cider vinegar and mustard dressing. Canned salmon with its soft bones brings **omega-3 and calcium**, and the chickpeas bring iron and fibre.

ingredients.note: drained, skin and soft bones left in

steps: Whisk the vinegar, mustard and olive oil with a spoonful of water and the pepper.

Rinse and drain the chickpeas. Wash the apple, cabbage, carrot, spinach and parsley, then shred the cabbage, grate the carrot, cut the apple into matchsticks, thinly slice the onion and chop the parsley.
Toss the chickpeas, cabbage, carrot, apple, onion and parsley with most of the dressing. Toss the spinach with the rest and spread it in a wide bowl as a bed.
Pile the chickpea slaw onto the spinach, flake the salmon over the top and scatter the walnuts and sunflower seeds.
recipes.tip: Keep an opened tin covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days. Packing it? Use a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.

recipes.name: Warm mushroom, buckwheat and chickpea salad with kale and a firm egg
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Eastern European kasha with mushrooms, served as a warm salad
recipes.about: Browned mushrooms, nutty buckwheat and chickpeas with a firm egg, tossed with massaged kale, parsley and a mustard-lemon dressing. The chickpeas and egg bring **protein and choline**, and the mushrooms bring B vitamins.
steps: Put the egg in a small pot of cold water, bring to a boil and simmer 10 to 11 minutes until the yolk is completely firm. Cool in cold water and peel.

Rinse the buckwheat and simmer it in about twice its volume of water with a lid on for 12 minutes. Take it off the heat, let it steam 5 minutes, then spread it in a shallow container to cool slightly.
Meanwhile, sear the mushrooms in a hot dry skillet for 5 minutes until browned, then add a little of the oil and the garlic for 30 seconds.
Whisk the lemon juice, mustard, the rest of the oil, a pinch of iodized salt and pepper. Wash, stem and finely slice the kale and rub it with a spoonful of the dressing for a minute to soften it.

Toss the buckwheat, mushrooms, drained chickpeas, kale, onion and parsley with the rest of the dressing and scatter the chopped walnuts and almonds on top. Quarter the egg and add it cold. Eat warm or at room temperature.
recipes.tip: Cook the buckwheat the night before, cool it within 1 hour in a shallow container and refrigerate. Use it within 3 days. Packing it? Keep the egg in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.

recipes.name: Chicken, chickpea and mushroom masala with sweet potato and spinach
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian chole and chicken masala, with mushrooms, sweet potato and spinach
recipes.about: Chicken, chickpeas and mushrooms simmered with sweet potato in a tomato, ginger and garam masala sauce, with spinach stirred in at the end and a spoon of cool yogurt. The chickpeas and spinach bring **iron and folate**, the sweet potato brings vitamin A, and the lemon helps you absorb the iron.
steps: Warm the oil in a wide pot over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken pieces for 4 minutes, turning, then move them to a clean plate. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken.
In the same pot, cook the chopped onion 4 minutes, then the mushrooms 5 minutes more until browned. Stir in the grated garlic, garam masala, turmeric, cumin and ginger for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the crushed tomatoes, the sweet potato, a pinch of iodized salt and enough water to nearly cover. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook 12 minutes.
Return the chicken, add the drained chickpeas and simmer, uncovered, 6 minutes more, until the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) and the sweet potato is tender.
Stir in the washed spinach until wilted, then the lemon juice. Serve topped with the yogurt and chopped parsley.
recipes.tip: For heat, add a pinch of chili powder or a slit green chili with the spices.

recipes.name: Orange with sunflower seeds
recipes.about: Juicy orange segments with sunflower seeds. Sunflower seeds bring **vitamin E**, which is one of the harder vitamins to reach.
steps: Wash and peel the orange and split it into segments.
Serve with the sunflower seeds.

recipes.name: Greek yogurt with orange and almonds
recipes.about: Thick Greek yogurt with juicy orange pieces and chopped almonds. It brings **protein and calcium**, and the almonds bring vitamin E.
steps: Wash and peel the orange, then chop it into pieces.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and top with the orange and chopped almonds.

recipes.name: Pear with almonds
recipes.about: A juicy pear with almonds. The pear skin brings **fibre**, and the almonds bring vitamin E.
steps: Wash the pear and slice it.
Serve with the almonds.

recipes.name: Pear with walnuts
recipes.about: A juicy pear with crunchy walnuts. The walnuts add **omega-3 fats** and a good bite to the sweet fruit.
steps: Wash the pear and slice it.
Serve with the walnuts.

recipes.name: Banana with walnuts and cinnamon
recipes.about: A ripe banana with walnuts and a dusting of cinnamon. The banana brings **potassium** and the walnuts bring omega-3 fats.
steps: Slice the banana into a bowl.
Top with the walnuts and cinnamon.

recipes.name: Greek yogurt with cinnamon and walnuts
recipes.about: Thick Greek yogurt with a dusting of cinnamon and chopped walnuts. It brings **protein and calcium** with a little crunch.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl.
Top with the cinnamon and the chopped walnuts.

recipes.name: Apple slices with walnuts and cinnamon
recipes.about: Crisp apple slices with walnuts and a dusting of cinnamon. The apple skin brings **fibre**, and the walnuts bring omega-3 fats.
steps: Wash the apple, cut it into slices and dust with the cinnamon.
Serve with the walnuts.

recipes.name: Banana with almonds
recipes.about: A ripe banana with a small handful of almonds. The banana brings **potassium** and the almonds bring vitamin E and magnesium.
steps: Slice the banana into a bowl.
Top with the almonds.

recipes.name: Smoky roasted chickpeas
recipes.about: Crunchy chickpeas roasted with smoked paprika and cumin, ready in 25 minutes. A handful gives you **plant protein and fibre**.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Drain the chickpeas, rinse and pat them very dry with a clean towel.
Toss with the oil, paprika, cumin and a pinch of iodized salt on a tray.
Roast 25 minutes, shaking the tray once or twice, until crisp. They crisp more as they cool.
recipes.tip: Best the day they are made. Cool completely before storing in a loosely covered container.

recipes.name: Carrot sticks with white bean and sage dip
recipes.about: Creamy white beans mashed with lemon, garlic and a little sage for dipping crunchy carrot. It is a snack with **fibre and plant protein** in it.
steps: Mash the beans with the lemon juice, olive oil, grated garlic, sage, a pinch of iodized salt and a spoonful of water until fairly smooth.
Wash and peel the carrots and cut them into sticks. Serve with the dip.
recipes.tip: Make a small batch of dip and keep it covered in the fridge up to 3 days.

recipes.name: Walnut, almond and seed mix
recipes.about: A small handful of walnuts, almonds, pumpkin seeds and sunflower seeds. Together they bring **vitamin E, omega-3, iron and magnesium**.
steps: Stir the walnuts, almonds, pumpkin seeds and sunflower seeds together.
Keep a small portion in a jar or bag.
